newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai shares fall at noon on bank stock ban.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai shares fall at noon on bank stock ban.

text.p: Shanghai's A and B shares fell sharply at midday on Friday after China's central bank announced a ban on state banks trading on the stock markets and the state debt repurchase and spot secondary markets, brokers said.
The domestic A share index lost 78.189 points or 5.5 percent to 1,343.246 points and the foreign currency B share index lost 2.341 points or 2.62 percent to 86.865 points.
The People's Bank announced the ban late Thursday, ordering the banks to offset their existing stock postions in 10 days.
Brokers said the ban would damage market sentiment and sharply reduce liquidity on the stock markets.
"Market sentiment has been hit by the ban," one A share trader said.
"The A index is likely to fall by around 20 percent in the next few days," he said.
"Half the liquidity on China's A share markets is believed to come from state banks trading on the state debt repo market," said a second trader.
"The ban will heavily cut money supply on the stock markets, in particular the primary (share issue) market," he said.
Brokers said they expected the A share market would be harder hit than the B share market.
"There is much less illegal money on the B share markets because foreigners dominate trading," one broker said.

At midday, volume on the A share market was at 466.6 million shares, valued at 7.2 billion yuan. In contrast, B market volume was only 10.5 million shares worth $8.4 million, indicating selling was heavier on the A market, brokers said.
Among B shares, Shanghai Dazhong Taxi Co was the biggest loser on profit-taking, falling $0.056 or 5.96 percent to $0.884 on volume of 508,500 shares.
Many A shares hit the 10-percent limit-down level with newcomer Gezhouba losing 2.27 yuan to 20.39 yuan.
